messages:
maya: heads-up — seeing a 15-25% p50 regression on multi-GPU runs with TP=2 + fused attention after yesterday's kernel picker change.
jonas: which workloads? seq lenses, batch size?
maya: repro on conv eval set and our locale model. seq=128/256, batch=4/8. The regression shows up when QKV all-gather happens.
liam: can you paste the nsys slice?
maya: paste below (trimmed):
```
Time (ms)  Kernel                         GPU  Comm
0.32       fused_attn_qkv_optim           0    compute
0.85       nccl_allgather_qkv             0    comm (nvlink)
6.3        fallback_qkv_shard             1    compute
```
Notice rank1 stalls 5-6ms waiting for a slow allgather, then runs fallback kernel.
priya: fallback_qkv_shard? kernel selector chose non-fused when allgather latency > X?
maya: yes. kernel picker has heuristic: if allgather latency > 1ms or streams out of order -> pick contiguous fallback that expects local qkv. That avoids correctness issues but kills perf when it happens intermittently.
jonas: do we know why allgather latency spiked? link bandwidth, small message sizes, or nccl algo?
liam: on NvLink chain with TP=2 we saw an extra copy introduced by KV-cache prefetch in stream C which hit the same GPU as nccl and serialized.
maya: here's a minimal trace of stream ordering:
```
streamA: compute(qkv_pack) -> eventE
streamB: ncclAllgather.start -> waits for eventE? (no) -> race
streamC: prefetch_kv -> cudaMemcpyAsync -> records eventF
streamB: cudaStreamWaitEvent(eventF) // forces cross-stream sync later
```
That wait seems to push the allgather behind the prefetch copy for certain batch alignments.
priya: could be our prefetch moving into the comm stream; we intended prefetch to be on a non-blocking copy stream.
jonas: suggestion: make nccl operations use a dedicated comm stream and ensure we enqueue prefetch copies on a separate stream with cudaStreamSynchronize semantics that don't create implicit waits. Also consider using ncclGroupStart/End to fuse ops.
liam: also saw kernel selector toggling because qkv memory layout becomes noncontiguous after a transpose in the batching path for odd batch sizes (batch=5,7). The fused kernel only supports contiguous layout.
maya: yes — interleaved batching heuristic caused a small stride for qkv when batch%2 !=0, fallback chosen. Combined with allgather delay that's the regression.
priya: two short-term patches: 1) ensure prefetch uses non-blocking pinned memcpy on streamP and record event to comm stream only if necessary; 2) tweak kernel selector to allow fused path for common stride patterns (detect simple stride=3 interleave).
jonas: can we add a telemetry flag to count occurrences where selector flips kernel at runtime? would help quantify scope.
liam: i'll add a counter: KERNEL_FLIP_{from}_{to} with tags (seq_len,batch,rank). can emit to perf logs.
maya: for immediate mitigation, rolling back the heuristic change re: allgather latency threshold brought p50 back to baseline in canary. infra-bot: rollout 1.3.9-rollback applied to canary cluster.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollout 1.3.9-rollback -> canary (3 nodes) succeeded :white_check_mark:
priya: added a tiny patch to prefetch stream assignment in branch fix/prefetch-stream. PR up for review: https://git.redwood/infer/pulls/738
jonas: let's also benchmark NCCL algorithm choices. try NCCL_ALGO=ring vs tree for these message sizes.
liam: noted. running sweep now: `NCCL_ALGO=ring NCCL_MIN_NTHREADS=8 python -m rdinfer.bench --model local-7b --tp 2 --batch 8 --seq 128`
maya: thanks. I'll collect perf counters and attach a small flamegraph. Also adding an e2e test for odd batch compacting path to prevent regressing selector logic again.
priya: agree. leaving a comment on PR about telemetry tags.
jonas: good thread — next steps: (1) merge prefetch-stream PR, (2) push kernel selector loosen for stride=3 contig, (3) nccl algo sweep results.
maya: i'll follow up in tomorrow standup with numbers. :sparkles:
